decisions.reason: Separate LED and sensor control replaces the current policy of disabling the entire shared 5V rail whenever the LEDs are not needed.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I added separate control for led vs sensors so we might not need shifter

value_updates.led_standby_power_policy: LED power is controlled separately from sensor power

decisions.reason: Separate power control does not change the daughterboard's LED count, board form, addressability, or selected LED part.
The current interface exposes one 5V_EN signal, but the source does not specify whether separate LED and sensor control requires an additional interboard signal or is implemented locally.
Separating control of loads on the 5V supply does not necessarily change which rails are monitored or the selected monitoring device.
The decision concerns separate control of 5V LED and sensor loads and does not alter DCDC1's 3.3V regulation role.
The standalone USB requirement supplies the 3.3V rail, while the source only changes control separation for LED and sensor power.
Separate LED power control does not change how charge status is displayed or the dedicated charge-LED interface.
The source does not require any change to the sensor board's connector count, connector types, or documented power and signal pinouts.
Separate sensor power control does not alter the SPS30 connector, 5V supply requirement, I2C signals, or SEL connection.
The LED-versus-sensor power-control change does not affect USB enumeration, programming, or D+/D- routing.
Separate LED and sensor control may require another GPIO assignment, but the source does not identify the new control signal or say whether GPIO5 remains assigned to 5V_EN.
Separate downstream load control does not change the AXP2101 battery input range or its role as the normal system power source.
